title: School Liaison
intro: We support military families by prioritizing the educational needs of their children, providing resources, and ensuring smooth transitions between schools.

sections.heading: Connect with a School Liaison
sections.markdown: Getting connected is easy.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.markdown:
Members of our military community with school-aged children (PreK-12) are eligible to access the services provided by the School Liaison Program.

* Active-duty Service Members
* DoD Civilian
* National Guard
* Reserves
* Retirees

sections.heading: Getting Started
sections.markdown:
Figuring out schools during a move or facing school-related questions can be tough, but you don't have to do it alone. Your School Liaison is here to help make things smoother for you and your family.

**Contact the School Liaison**
Reach out to your local School Liaison office for personalized support.

**Schedule a Consultation**
Set up a meeting or phone call with the School Liaison to discuss your child's needs, school options, and any concerns you may have regarding the transition.

**Collect Important Documents**
Maintain important records, such as school transcripts, report cards, individual education plans (IEPs), and any other documentation that will assist the School Liaison in supporting your family.

**Learn About Local School Options**
The School Liaison can provide details on the local school districts, private schools, charter schools, homeschooling, and other alternative education options to help you make an informed decision.

**Explore Available Resources**
The School Liaison can direct you to resources such as tutoring services, scholoarships, extracurricular activities, and other programs.

**Stay Connected**
Maintain communication with the School Liaison throughout your assignment to receive ongoing support and updates on educational opportunities for your child.

Don't hesitate to contact your School Liaison, who is ready to support your family's educational journey!

sections.heading: Our Support
sections.markdown:
The School Liaison will provide you with important information, assist with enrollment, navigate grade and credit transfers, and ensure that your child receives support to connect to their new environment. The School Liaison can also help you facilitate communication with principals, teachers, or other school staff, making your child's transition smoother.

Empowering you with the information you need, they ensure you can make informed decisions about your child's education and be their strongest advocate.

Your School Liaison is the critical link between families, commands, communities, and schools.

* Promotes and enhances education services and programs.
* Provides incoming families with information regarding Local Education Agencies.
* Leverage the Interstate Compact and assist with grade/credit transferability.
* Ensure children/youth and LEAs are supported by military community.
* Facilitate command sponsored Adopt-a-School opportunities.

sections.heading: Resources for Military Families
sections.markdown: Additional services to strengthen and support military families.

sections.heading: Adjusting to Changes
sections.markdown:
Moving to a new duty station can be challenging for military families, especially for children adjusting to a new school and environment.

[Community Counseling](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/prevention-and-counseling/community-counseling) provides support to ease this transition by offering emotional support, stress management strategies, and adjustment counseling. Counselors help families navigate the challenges of relocation, offering guidance on coping with change, building resilience, and connecting with local resources.

Through individual and family counseling, the program helps create a smooth transition, strengthening the overall well-being of military families.

Life Skills Development Resources:

* Relationship Concerns
* Work Stressors
* Life Stressors
* Trauma
* EAS/PCS and Challenges Related to Transition
* Grief and Loss
* Sadness
* Worry
* Deployment Cycle Stressors and Reintegration
* Adjustment
* Crisis Intervention
* Sleep Hygiene
* Parent-Child Communication

sections.heading: Budgeting for Your Move
sections.markdown:
[Personal Financial Management](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/personal-financial-management) is here to support your military family during your move to another duty station. From budgeting for relocation expenses to understanding allowances, and managing housing costs, our experts provide guidance to help you stay financially secure throughout your transition. Connect with us to plan ahead and make your move easier!

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

* Blended Retirement System (BRS)
* Car Buying
* Consumer Awareness
* Continuation Pay
* Couple Financial Counseling
* Credit Report and Credit Score Analysis Saving and Investing
* Credit / Debt Management
* Developing a Spending Plan
* Financial Education Action Points (FEAP)
* Individual Financial Counseling
* Major Purchases
* Military Pay & Benefits
* Retirement Planning
* Survivor Benefits Plan
* Thrift Savings Plan
* Understanding Military Retirement Benefits

sections.heading: Libraries
sections.markdown:
The [Library](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/libraries) is a great resource for families and school-age children, offering books, educational programs, and activities that support learning and growth. Whether you're looking for homework help, fun storytimes, or a quiet place to read and explore, the Library provides a welcoming space for children to develop their love of learning. Stop by and discover all the ways we support your family!

**Life Skills Development Resources:**

* **Children's Collection:** A diverse selection of picture books, chapter books, movies, and audiobooks designed for young readers.
* **Summer Reading Program:** Featuring free activities and incentives to encourage a love of reading during the summer months.
* **Storytime Kits:** Themed kits that include books and activities, allowing families to enjoy storytime at their convenience.
* **Educational Programs and Activities:** Various events and workshops that enrich your children's learning experiences.
* **Access to Digital Resources:** Online materials, including e-books and educational databases, to support learning and exploration. Vist the [DoD MWR Virtual Library](https://marines.dodmwrlibraries.org./).

sections.heading: Before & After School Care
sections.markdown:
[School Age Care](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/school-age-care) (SAC) programs support your military family with after-school care, learning opportunities in a safe environment. Whether you need care before or after school, help with homework, or a nurturing home environment for your child, these programs provide safe and reliable options.

**School Age Care (SAC)**
SAC offers child care for kids in kindergarten through age 12, giving them a structured and fun environment when they're not in school. You can rely on SAC for:

* **After-School Support** – Your child will have a safe place to go before and after school, during holidays, and over the summer. They'll enjoy fun activities, make friends, and stay active while you focus on your work or military duties.
* **Educational Services** – SAC provides homework help, tutoring, and learning activities that support what your child is doing in school.
* **Support for Military Families** – If your schedule changes due to training or deployment, SAC offers flexible hours so your child always has consistent care.

Register for School Age Care at [MilitaryChildCare.com](https://public.militarychildcare.csd.disa.mil/mcc-central/mcchome#/).

sections.heading: Exceptional Family Members
sections.markdown:
The [Exceptional Family Member Program](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/exceptional-family-member-program) (EFMP) is dedicated to supporting military families by ensuring they have access to the resources and services needed to thrive. We understand that navigating military life with a family member who has special needs can be challenging, which is why EFMP works closely with the School Liaison Program to provide seamless support for educational transitions, school advocacy, and special education resources. Together, we help families find the best-fit schools, understand their rights, and access individualized services that promote academic success and overall well-being.

How EFMP Supports Families:

* **Lending Library** – Borrow sensory tools, assistive devices, and educational materials to support learning and development at home.
* **Respite Care Services** – Provides temporary relief for caregivers, ensuring they have time to recharge while their loved one receives quality care.
* **Assignment Coordination** – Ensures that families are stationed at locations with appropriate medical and educational services for their exceptional family members.
* **Advocacy & Support** – Assists families in navigating the special education system, including IEPs (Individualized Education Programs) .
* **Workshops & Resources** – Offers educational sessions on topics like navigating the EFMP process, advocacy skills, and community resources.

By working together, EFMP and the School Liaison help ensure that your child receives the support they need—at home, in school, and throughout their military journey. We are here to support you every step of the way!

sections.heading: Family Child Care
sections.markdown:
[Family Child Care](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/child-and-youth/family-child-care) (FCC) gives you in-home child care from trained and certified providers, often military spouses, in military housing. This program is great if you prefer a smaller, home-like setting for your child. FCC offers:

* **Home-Based Care** – Your child will be cared for in a safe, nurturing home setting with small group sizes and personalized attention.
* **Educational Activities** – FCC providers include age-appropriate learning, playtime, and rest in their daily schedules, helping your child grow and develop.
* **Flexible Child Care** – Whether you need full-time, part-time, or overnight care, FCC providers can work with your schedule, making it easier to handle deployments or unpredictable work hours.

sections.heading: Information, Referral, and Relocation
sections.markdown:
Moving to a new duty station can be overwhelming, but you don't have to navigate it alone. [Information, Referral, and Relocation](https://quantico.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/information-referral-and-relocation) (IR&R) services are here to help you and your family transition smoothly and feel at home in your new community.

**Here's how IR&R can support you:**

* **Relocation Assistance** – Get guidance on housing, base services, child care, and community resources to establish stability for your family.
* **Local School Information** – Connect you to the School Liaison, educational resources, enrollment requirements, and district policies to ensure a smooth school transition.
* **Welcome Aboard Resources** – Access newcomer checklists, area guides, and personalized referrals to help you get familiar with your new surroundings.
* **Lending Locker** – Borrow temporary household items to make settling in easier while you wait for your belongings to arrive.

Wherever your journey takes you, IR&R is here to provide the information and resources you need to make your transition as smooth as possible.

sections.heading: Marine Corps Family Team Building
sections.markdown:
[Marine Corps Family Team Building (MCFTB)](https://www.usmc-mccs.org/marine-family-support/military-family-life/marine-corps-family-team-building) is designed to enhance the resilience, readiness, and well-being of all members of the Marine Corps community, including service members, spouses, children, extended family members, command leaders, units, and support personnel.

How to get started with MCFTB:

1. Identify Individual Needs: Determine what specific support or resources you or your family require. MCFTB offers a variety of workshops, classes, and resources tailored to different needs, including deployment support, spouse education and career assistance, relationship-enhancement, and more.
   
   MCFTB professionals can help you identify your specific needs.
   
2. Connect with MCFTB: Reach out to MCFTB professionals either in person or by phone. They can provide guidance on available programs, workshops, and resources that best suit your needs.
   
3. Attend Workshops and Classes: Participate in MCFTB workshops, classes, and events relevant to your situation. These could include pre-deployment briefs, relationship-enhancement classes, pre-marital and marital workshops, relocation assistance workshops, family readiness seminars, financial planning classes, and more.
   
4. Connect with Other Families: Take advantage of opportunities to connect with other Marine Corps families through MCFTB-sponsored events, support groups, and social media platforms. Building connections with other families can provide valuable support and camaraderie.

sections.heading: FAQs
sections.markdown: Find information and get quick answers to common questions.

sections.heading: What does the School Liaison do?
sections.markdown: The program helps military families navigate the education system and assists with school transitions, special education services, and local school information.

sections.heading: Who can use the School Liaison?
sections.markdown: The program is available to active-duty military families, National Guard and Reserve members on active orders, DoD civilians, and retired service members with school-aged children, whether families live on or off base.

sections.heading: How can the School Liaison help during a PCS move?
sections.markdown: School Liaisons provide resources for enrolling in new schools, transferring credits, and ensuring a smooth transition. They can also help find information on local schools, extracurricular activities, and educational support.

sections.heading: What educational resources are available through the School Liaison?
sections.markdown: School Liaisons provide access to resources such as tutoring, special education information, and connections to homeschooling or virtual school options.

sections.heading: Can the School Liaison assist with special education needs?
sections.markdown: Yes, School Liaisons can help families understand the special education process, connect with local resources, and support children with IEPs (Individualized Education Programs) or 504 Plans.

sections.heading: Can School Liaisons help with college readiness?
sections.markdown: Yes, School Liaisons provide resources for college planning, scholarships, and navigating the college admissions process.

sections.heading: Do School Liaisons only work with DoDEA schools?
sections.markdown: No, School Liaisons support families regardless of whether their children attend public, private, DoDEA schools, or homeschool families. They are knowledgeable about all education options available in the local area.
